children.text: In recent years, Germany has been continuously working on its immigration policy and trying to simplify labor market access for immigrants and foreign workers, driven by a shortage of skilled labor. As a result, the large number of active job vacancies remains a major challenge for the country.

A survey conducted by the Munich-based IFO Institute found that 87% of family businesses are experiencing a shortage of qualified personnel - EURES, Report on Labour Shortages and Surpluses (2022). Professions facing shortages mainly include software, healthcare, construction, and engineering trades.

Against this backdrop, opportunities are opening up for foreigners aiming to live and work in Germany. Because of the labor shortage in Germany, foreign workers have the opportunity to apply for a work visa, for which the main requirement is holding the relevant qualification.

According to data from the Economic Research Institute (ERI), the average pay for people employed in agriculture is 35,626 euros per year and 17 euros per hour. Annual pay for those employed in forestry is 36,791 euros per year, and 18 euros per hour. Pay for people employed in construction is 44,052 euros per year, and 21 euros per hour. As for drivers, their average pay is 28,276 euros per year and 14 euros per hour.

Among Germany's highest-paying professions, medicine ranks first, with doctors earning an average annual salary of €71,600–€101,690; second place goes to pilots (€93,499), and third to sales management (€82,392).

In order for a Georgian citizen to be able to work in Germany, they must hold a German work visa. If you're interested in working in Germany and want to obtain a work visa, our team will provide you with full visa support. Keep in mind that before starting the visa process, an invitation from an employer and holding the relevant qualification are important requirements.
